source_evidence: if you are saving for a short-term goal, five years or less, you don’t want to choose risky investments, because when it’s time to sell, you may have to take a loss.
question: How can your investment time horizon affect whether you choose risky investments?
answer: Your time horizon matters because you may have to sell when you need the money. For a short-term goal of five years or less, the source cautions against risky investments because you could have to sell at a loss. For a much longer horizon, such as 35 years until retirement, you may consider riskier investments.
